approachQuestion.prompt: A circular conveyor has n stations with integer capacities, possibly repeated. For each station return the distance to the first strictly larger capacity encountered by moving forward around the ring, examining at most the other n-1 stations. Return 0 if none qualifies. Example: [5, 1, 4] returns [0, 1, 1]; [2, 2] returns [0, 0]. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Scan virtual positions t=0 through 2n-1, reading capacity[t mod n]. Pop unresolved original indices while their values are smaller, storing t-index as the distance. Push index t only during the first lap. Leave unanswered outputs as 0.
options.feedback: Each original index is added once. The second lap supplies wrapped successors; a value cannot resolve its own equal value, and any larger value seen after a full lap would already have been encountered earlier.

options.text: Scan once, resolving smaller earlier positions, and leave all remaining positions at 0.
options.feedback: Wrapped answers are missed. For [5, 1, 4], station 2 reaches the larger station 0 at distance 1.

options.text: Find one global maximum and report the forward distance to it for every station with smaller capacity.
options.feedback: The first larger station need not be a global maximum. In [5, 1, 4], station 1 first reaches 4 at distance 1, not 5 at distance 2.

options.text: From every station walk forward for at most n-1 steps until finding a larger capacity.
options.feedback: It is correct but repeats almost a full lap for every station when all capacities are equal, causing quadratic work.

feedback.reason: Model wraparound without creating duplicate unresolved candidates.
details: Use one unresolved-index stack initialized empty and an answer array initialized to zero. Process two virtual laps, resolving smaller top values using virtual distance. Push original indices only in the first lap.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For two-lap-resolution, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the number of stations. The ring is accessed by modular indexing, with no duplicated input array. The output array is excluded.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two scans and one lifetime per original index give linear work.
details: The virtual scan has 2n iterations. Each original index is pushed once and popped at most once, so total work is linear. Equal capacities can retain n unresolved indices, giving linear auxiliary space.
